title: What If the Air Had 35 Percent Oxygen?

scenes.text: What if the air held 35 percent oxygen instead of 21? Earth has been there.
About 300 million years ago, in the Carboniferous, oxygen may have reached 30 to 35 percent.
Dragonfly relatives called Meganisoptera had wingspans around 70 centimeters, more than two feet.
Scientists long thought the extra oxygen let insects grow that big, though a newer Nature study questions it.
Higher oxygen may also have fueled enormous forest fires.
Giant insects, wilder fires, and a mystery scientists are still arguing about.
